answer: Agents must stake a unique pigment sample harvested only at a physical jetty during a timed window; the sample is sealed in a velvet pouch whose cryptographic hash is posted on-chain. Verification requires presenting the physical pouch for multi-party inspection before any identity is activated. An attacker needs exclusive physical access to the jetty, timed presence, and non-duplicable pigment material for every fake identity, making large-scale Sybil farms capital- and logistics-prohibitive while honest agents pay only once.
